chunks: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abi al-Khattab narrated to us from al-Hakam b. Miskin al-Thaqafi from Abu al-Ala al-Khaffaf from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He said:
Whoever prays Maghrib and then follows it up without speaking until he prays two units, they are recorded for him in Illiyyin. And if he prays four units, an accepted Hajj is recorded for him.

key_terms.حجة مبرورة: An accepted pilgrimage (Hajj), one free of sin
key_terms.عقب: To follow up (ta'qib), performing voluntary acts after obligatory prayer
key_terms.عليين: Illiyyin, the register of the righteous in the highest heavens (Quran 83:18-21)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward of praying voluntary units after Maghrib prayer?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (as) describes the great reward of performing voluntary prayers (nawafil) immediately after the Maghrib prayer without speaking in between. Two units earn a place in Illiyyin (the register of the righteous, referenced in Quran 83:18), while four units earn the equivalent reward of an accepted pilgrimage. This encourages maintaining focus and devotion in the transition between obligatory and voluntary worship.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abi’l Khattab narrated to us from al-Hakam b. Miskin al-Thaqai from Abi’l `Ala’ al-Khaffaf from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad (as). He said:
He who prays Maghrib and follows it up by praying two units, without speaking in between, shall be among the elect (`iliyyin). If he prays four units, he shall have an accepted Hajj recorded for him.
